summary: The Council of the Great City Schools expresses support for modernizing the E-Rate program but opposes any suggestion to limit or sunset the program due to the daily need for internet access in urban school districts. The text argues against limiting or ending E-Rate support for school districts, emphasizing the importance of internet access for educational infrastructure and the potential increase in costs for schools. The text discusses the impact of budget cuts on school districts, including the need to reprogram funding from other areas to backfill any loss of support resulting from changes to E-Rate. It highlights the ongoing increases in operational and infrastructure costs and the enrollment declines, leading to system-wide budget cuts.
